title: Elementary functions: `StrictMath` (fdlibm) for exp, logs, pow; `java.lang.Math` for the rest
verdict: exp, ln, log10, pow: fdlibm, the same everywhere; sqrt, trig: `Math`, within 1 ulp, may vary
description: `exp`, `expm1`, `ln`, `log10`, `log1p`, `log(b, x)` and `power` call `java.lang.StrictMath`, whose results are fdlibm's bit for bit on every JVM. `log2(x)` is `StrictMath.log(x) / StrictMath.log(2)`, two roundings: it can be an ulp off the correctly rounded log₂. `sqrt`, `sin`, `cos`, `tan`, `asin`, `acos`, `atan`, `atan2`, `cbrt` and the hyperbolic functions call `java.lang.Math`, which the JIT may replace with intrinsics within 1 ulp of the exact result (Java's spec), so the last bit can differ between platforms and JVMs. `sqrt` is correctly rounded on every JVM.
A `FLOAT` argument is widened to `DOUBLE` and the result is a `DOUBLE` (spark-fp32).
reference: The reference computes these with Lean's `Float` (the platform's libm, in double) and fixes `rounding: TIE_TO_EVEN`; the last bits are each engine's (#54). sverify's ε (#85) per function and platform comes from these facts.

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_spark` runs each query four times on one local session: with `spark.sql.ansi.enabled` true and false, on the folded path (the optimizer evaluates a query over `VALUES` on the driver) and on the codegen path (`ConvertToLocalRelation` and `ConstantFolding` excluded, so the query runs as a job with whole-stage code generation). probes.json keeps one result per ANSI setting where the two paths agree. Spark 4.3.0 (pyspark 4.3.0), Java 21.0.12, Linux x86_64, `local[2]`, session time zone UTC, `spark.sql.timestampType=TIMESTAMP_NTZ`.
